The left-hand column represents the ﬁ rst nucleotide base for each codon in the
row, while the row across the top of the table represents the second nucleotide
base in each codon. All 64 triplet codons have meaning, with 61 of them encoding
amino acids and 3 serving as STOP codons to signal the end of a coding sequence.
Methionine (Met) is always the ﬁ rst amino acid in a protein, and its codon, there-
fore, serves as a START codon. Standard amino acid abbreviations are as follows:
• Ala, alanine
• Asn, asparagine
• Asp, aspartic acid
• Arg, arginine
• Cys, cysteine
• Gln, glutamine
• Glu, glutamic acid
• Gly, glycine
• His, histidine
• Ile, isoleucine
• Leu, leucine
• Lys, lysine
• Met, methionine
• Phe, phenylalanine
• Pro, proline
• Ser, serine
• Thr, threonine
• Try, tryptophan
• Tyr, tyrosine
• Val, valine
